text: She sat down, looked at me, and asked how I was coping at home before touching the chart.
Prescription was refilled on time. Parking was easy.
He cut me off mid-sentence and typed the whole visit.
The doctor noticed my voice shaking and paused the exam to ask what worried me most.
Front desk was rude, but the doctor apologized for the wait and asked about my mother by name.
Visit lasted six minutes. He knows his medicine, I guess.
She explained the biopsy twice, then asked if I wanted my husband called in first.
Billing charged me twice. Avoid this office.
He said 'lots of patients feel that way' and moved on to dosage.
When I cried she handed me tissues and waited without checking the clock.
Good surgeon. Scar healed clean.
The nurse was kind; the doctor barely looked up from the screen.
He remembered my dog died last year and asked how the house feels now.
Told me to lose weight and left. No plan, no questions.
She called me personally with the results on a Friday evening so I would not worry all weekend.
Wait time forty minutes. Magazines old.
He answered every question but never once asked one back.
The doctor laughed off my pain scale answer as dramatic.
After the bad news she stayed an extra ten minutes and wrote her cell number on the card.
Standard checkup, in and out, no complaints.
He asked what the diagnosis would mean for my job before I raised it.
Competent but cold. Like talking to a well-trained kiosk.
She adjusted the plan when I said I could not afford the brand drug, without making me feel small.
The office smells like lavender. Five stars.
He noticed I flinched at the needle and talked me through each step.
Great with my kid, terrible with paperwork.
She said there was nothing more she could do and shrugged.
The doctor asked about my sleep, my appetite, and finally how my marriage was holding up.
Efficient. Correct. Forgettable.
He phoned the pharmacy himself when I said the copay confused me.
